topics.title: A. Definition of Claim — §101(5), Debt and Bankruptcy Consequences
topics.description: Why rights to payment enter claims process, how debts correlate and what happens when an obligation is not a claim.

entries.title: §101(5)(A): extremely broad right to payment
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: A claim includes any right to payment, whether reduced to judgment or not, liquidated/unliquidated, fixed/contingent, matured/unmatured, disputed/undisputed, legal/equitable, secured/unsecured.
entries.laymanExplanation: Creditor's right to get money can count even if payment is years away, amount uncertain or debtor contests it.
entries.legalExplanation: 1978 Code moved beyond narrow pre-Code provability; §101(5)(A) broadly includes future/uncertain monetary obligations subject to temporal and constitutional limitations.
entries.examApplication: Use §101(5) exact modifiers when spotting not-yet-due, contingent tort or breach.
entries.examTrap: 'Not yet payable' isn't automatically 'not a claim'.

entries.title: §101(5)(B): equitable remedy giving rise to right to payment
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: A right to an equitable remedy for breach of performance is a bankruptcy claim insofar as the breach gives rise to an alternative right to payment, even though remedy may be an injunction or specific performance.
entries.laymanExplanation: An order to do something might be treated as debt if law lets claimant receive money instead.
entries.legalExplanation: Kovacs, Apex and Shearin test when obligation is a payment claim rather than unavoidable nonmonetary duty.
entries.examApplication: Identify state/federal law right to substitute damages, not merely defendant's cost to comply.
entries.examTrap: An expensive injunction is NOT automatically a right to payment.

entries.title: §101(12) debt = liability on a claim
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: The Code defines 'debt' as liability on a §101(5) claim; bankruptcy processes claims and discharges corresponding debts.
entries.laymanExplanation: A claim is creditor's side of equation; debt is debtor's liability side.
entries.legalExplanation: This definitional equivalence underlies §727, §1141 and plan-treatment analysis.
entries.examApplication: When asked dischargeability, first determine whether any statutory debt/claim exists.
entries.examTrap: Discharge isn't same thing as whether proof of claim was allowed.

entries.title: Four consequences of classification as claim
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Claim status determines discharge coverage, eligibility for estate distribution, scope of the collection stay and voting rights in Chapter 11.
entries.laymanExplanation: Calling something a bankruptcy claim gives its holder a place in the bankruptcy process—but often also subjects it to discharge.
entries.legalExplanation: A claim can be discharged even if not allowed; 'claim' ≠ 'allowed claim' and not all claims are actually paid.
entries.examTrap: Don't equate participation in payout with full payment or assumption claim is dischargeable under all conditions.

entries.title: If individual debtor's obligation is NOT a claim
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: A truly nonclaim obligation is not discharged and can't receive a bankruptcy distribution; it may remain enforceable against an individual after bankruptcy.
entries.laymanExplanation: If court says your duty wasn't 'debt,' creditor might get no bankruptcy check but could still enforce duty later.
entries.legalExplanation: Compare personal fresh start and equitable nonmonetary obligations after case.
entries.examApplication: Explain both inability to share distribution and postbankruptcy survival.
entries.examTrap: Nonclaim status is not always favorable to debtor.

entries.title: If corporate debtor's obligation is NOT a claim
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: For liquidating corporation, nonclaim receives no payout, and after dissolution often no surviving entity to enforce against; for reorganizing corporation, genuine nonclaim obligation remains enforceable in full against reorganized entity.
entries.laymanExplanation: If corporation disappears, no debtor to sue; if it survives Chapter 11, unprocessed obligation can survive too.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish Chapter 7 liquidation from Chapter 11 reorganization and the constitutional notice question.
entries.examApplication: Include debtor form and chapter in Grossman's-style analysis.
entries.examTrap: Can't apply individual Chapter 7 postdischarge enforcement consequences mechanically to corporation.

entries.title: Davenport and Johnson demonstrate broad inclusion
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Casebook refers to Davenport (criminal restitution treated as debt/claim) and Johnson v. Home State Bank (mortgage lien surviving Chapter 7 personal discharge is in rem claim eligible for Chapter 13); both illustrate breadth.
entries.laymanExplanation: Even court-ordered restitution or mortgage tied only to property may be a claim in legal sense.
entries.legalExplanation: References are casebook discussions, not complete opinion excerpts; separate §523 exceptions and later statutory amendments from bare claim characterization.
entries.examApplication: Classify in rem versus in personam liability and ask what discharges.
entries.examTrap: Claim existence does NOT establish dischargeability, especially criminal restitution.

topics.title: A. When Does a Claim Arise? Accrual, Conduct, Exposure and Relationship Tests
topics.description: Different circuit tests and constitutional notice distinct from the broad statutory claim definition.

entries.title: Petition date usually divides prepetition from new debts
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Whether a claim arose prepetition affects §362 stay, distribution and discharge. Torts may involve sale/exposure before filing but symptoms decades later.
entries.laymanExplanation: What happened before filing might cause an injury diagnosed ten years afterward.
entries.legalExplanation: The Code contemplates contingent and unmatured claims; bankruptcy date is not always state-law accrual date.
entries.examApplication: Construct timeline of prefiling manufacture, exposure, filing, confirmation, diagnosis and notice.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume discovery of illness creates first bankruptcy claim.

entries.title: Frenville accrual test (overruled in Third Circuit)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Under Frenville, a bankruptcy claim arose when state-law cause of action accrued, often at injury manifestation or third-party suit, even if defendant's conduct was much earlier. Grossman's overruled this restrictive test.
entries.laymanExplanation: Old approach waited until someone could sue under state law before it counted as a bankruptcy claim.
entries.legalExplanation: Frenville indemnification/accountant claim and Van Brunts later cancer manifestations exposed mismatch with contingent/unmatured language in §101(5).
entries.examApplication: Identify Frenville as rejected precedent in Third Circuit; discuss why §101(5) supports earlier claim recognition.
entries.examTrap: Never cite Frenville accrual as current controlling Third Circuit standard.

entries.title: Conduct test (Grady example)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Broad conduct approach looks to debtor's prefiling acts giving rise to liability, rather than manifestation; Grady involved prepetition use of Dalkon Shield with later injuries.
entries.laymanExplanation: If unsafe device implanted before filing, injury may create contingent prefiling claim even before symptoms.
entries.legalExplanation: Concern: an unlimited conduct-only theory could encompass future strangers who use product after case and lack notice.
entries.examApplication: Discuss Grady's known exposure compared with Piper criticism of universally encompassing manufactured products.
entries.examTrap: Conduct test doesn't solve future unknown claimant's constitutional notice by itself.

entries.title: Prepetition relationship/contact test (Lemelle, Piper)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Relationship theory generally requires prefiling connection such as purchase/use/exposure/impact/privity with product. Piper specifically allowed relationship before plan confirmation for products resulting from prepetition conduct.
entries.laymanExplanation: A defect in old manufactured airplane isn't enough if no one had any contact with it before bankruptcy confirmation, under Piper's framework.
entries.legalExplanation: Piper states two-part test: relationship from events prior to confirmation plus basis in debtor's prepetition design/manufacture/sale; Lemelle required evidence enabling identification/notice of claimants.
entries.examApplication: Compare an exposed worker, future purchaser who first buys after filing, and child not yet born.
entries.examTrap: Piper's preconfirmation variant isn't identical to absolute prepetition relationship wording.

entries.title: Grossman's exposure test in Third Circuit
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: An individual's claim arises when he or she is exposed prepetition to product or other debtor conduct giving rise to injury, even if injury manifests only later; court held 1977 asbestos exposure was claim origin.
entries.laymanExplanation: Someone inhaled asbestos long before bankruptcy; cancer diagnosis later doesn't undo earlier contingent claim.
entries.legalExplanation: Third Circuit en banc abandoned Frenville and adopted prepetition exposure test; distinct notice inquiry must follow.
entries.examApplication: Ask when exposure, not when doctor diagnosed mesothelioma or tort complaint filed.
entries.examTrap: Prepetition claim classification DOES NOT automatically mean debt actually discharged.

entries.title: Due process limits discharge of unknown future claims
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: A bankruptcy claim is not validly discharged without constitutionally adequate notice/opportunity to be heard; highly latent injuries raise special difficulty.
entries.laymanExplanation: You can't erase unknown person's rights without giving them a meaningful chance to be represented.
entries.legalExplanation: Grossman's reversed and remanded for separate notice inquiry; earlier notices only by general publication without asbestos focus, Van Brunt had no symptoms.
entries.examApplication: Analyze known/unknown creditor, exposure knowledge, publication adequacy, bar-date awareness, representation and constitutional fairness.
entries.examTrap: Never state Van Brunts' claim WAS discharged merely because Third Circuit called it prepetition.

entries.title: §524(g) future asbestos trust and channeling protections
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Section 524(g) permits qualifying asbestos debtor to channel present/future demands to funded trust, with future claimants' representative, fair/equitable plan treatment and specified supermajority vote; subject detailed statutory requirements.
entries.laymanExplanation: A company funds a common asbestos claims trust, even for people not diagnosed yet, instead of declaring them wiped out.
entries.legalExplanation: Manville Trust inspired statute; Grossman's plan did not create §524(g) trust and wasn't automatically protected by those procedures.
entries.examApplication: For mass asbestos plan ask whether representative, substantial trust funding, voting and fairness safeguards exist.
entries.examTrap: Do not apply §524(g) to every tort claim or presume it cures all unknown-claimant due process problems.

topics.title: A. In re Grossman's Inc. — Asbestos Exposure, Claim Timing and Due Process
topics.description: Complete Third Circuit en banc opinion and reversal of Frenville, claim versus discharge.

entries.title: In re Grossman's Inc., 607 F.3d 114 (3d Cir. 2010) (en banc)
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Third Circuit en banc expressly overruled Frenville. Prepetition exposure to asbestos product gave rise to contingent claim in 1977 under broad §101(5). But court did NOT determine whether discharge occurred: due-process adequacy of notice required separate factual analysis on remand. Reversed/remanded.
entries.laymanExplanation: For Third Circuit product liability, claim arises upon prepetition exposure to product/conduct underlying injury, even if later manifested; whether discharged also requires constitutional notice and proper procedures.
entries.legalExplanation: Sloviter reviewed §101(5) modifiers contingent/unmatured/unliquidated, rejected conflating bankruptcy claim with accrued state-law tort action. Compared Grady conduct test, Lemelle/Piper relationship and identifiability concerns; adopted prepetition exposure approach. Constitutional Mullane notice means unknown latent victim cannot be erased without meaningful procedure; §524(g) Manville model gives trust/future representative protections, absent from Grossman's plan. Lower courts never analyzed notice after ruling under Frenville.
entries.examApplication: Make a 1977→1997 petition/confirmation→2006 symptoms→2007 diagnosis timeline; identify separate statutory classification and due process tests; discuss §524(g) trust option.
entries.examTrap: Result is NOT that Van Brunts were definitively discharged; outcome of discharge left open for remand.
entries.sourceRole: Full case opinion excerpted in uploaded Chapter 5
entries.facts: Mary Van Brunt purchased allegedly asbestos-containing products from Grossman's in 1977 and was exposed during home remodel. Grossman's sought Chapter 11 in April 1997, knew it sold asbestos and risks, gave generic publication bar-date notice without future asbestos liability, and confirmed plan December 1997. Van Brunt first showed symptoms in 2006 and diagnosed mesothelioma 2007; she and spouse sued successor JELD-WEN. Bankruptcy and district courts applied Frenville state-law manifestation-accrual test to hold no 1997 claim/discharge.
entries.issue: When did a bankruptcy 'claim' arise for latent asbestos injury where exposure occurred before Chapter 11 but manifestation and diagnosis occurred years after confirmation; does finding a claim establish it was discharged?
entries.holding: Third Circuit en banc expressly overruled Frenville. Prepetition exposure to asbestos product gave rise to contingent claim in 1977 under broad §101(5). But court did NOT determine whether discharge occurred: due-process adequacy of notice required separate factual analysis on remand. Reversed/remanded.
entries.reasoning: Sloviter reviewed §101(5) modifiers contingent/unmatured/unliquidated, rejected conflating bankruptcy claim with accrued state-law tort action. Compared Grady conduct test, Lemelle/Piper relationship and identifiability concerns; adopted prepetition exposure approach. Constitutional Mullane notice means unknown latent victim cannot be erased without meaningful procedure; §524(g) Manville model gives trust/future representative protections, absent from Grossman's plan. Lower courts never analyzed notice after ruling under Frenville.
entries.rule: For Third Circuit product liability, claim arises upon prepetition exposure to product/conduct underlying injury, even if later manifested; whether discharged also requires constitutional notice and proper procedures.

entries.title: Why state accrual and bankruptcy claims differ
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: State-law tort action might be barred until injury manifests, yet bankruptcy claim may exist earlier as contingent/unmatured for federal proceedings.
entries.laymanExplanation: You may not be able to file a lawsuit today, yet bankruptcy may identify future legal exposure as a claim.
entries.legalExplanation: §101(5) would be emptied of breadth if court waited for state law final cause of action.
entries.examApplication: Contrast 1977 exposure and 2006 manifestation, old Frenville vs current exposure test.
entries.examTrap: Do not conflate right to sue today with right potentially payable later.

entries.title: Grossman's due process remand factors
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: On remand notice inquiry may consider exposure circumstances, victim awareness, bar date notice actual receipt, known vs unknown creditors, colorable claim and practical feasibility of future-claim trust.
entries.laymanExplanation: Was the asbestos victim reasonably identifiable or represented when bankruptcy plan purported to bind her?
entries.legalExplanation: Even a valid preconfirmation claim may survive if notice constitutionally inadequate; publication alone not universally enough for known creditors.
entries.examApplication: Include analysis of debtor knowledge that it sold asbestos, publication's omission, and absence of symptoms.
entries.examTrap: Don't mechanically equate notice to general public with adequate notice of future latent asbestos obligations.

entries.title: Lemelle, Chemetron, Piper: future claimant comparison
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: Lemelle mobile-home postconfirmation fatal fire without proven prepetition relationship, Piper future aircraft injury claimant, Chemetron plaintiff not yet born at discharge: notice/representation challenges differ from earlier exposure.
entries.laymanExplanation: Courts struggle with people nobody could identify at petition time.
entries.legalExplanation: Grossman's opinion describes authorities to explain competing narrower definition and direct due-process approach.
entries.examApplication: Compare claimant first exposed before vs after filing/confirmation, and if future rep appointed.
entries.examTrap: These referenced authorities are not full opinions excerpted in this chapter.

entries.title: The distinction between legal claim and ultimate discharge
entries.source: Tabb & Brubaker, Bankruptcy Law: Principles, Policies, and Practice, 5th ed. (2021), user-uploaded complete Chapter 5, Unsecured Claims, §A, In re Grossman's Inc.; section-based locations (ebook lacks printed page markers)
entries.summary: §101(5) defines what may be addressed, but §1141 confirmation discharge must also satisfy due process notice and statutory conditions.
entries.laymanExplanation: A file may be listed in bankruptcy, yet cannot be legally erased if holder never had proper warning.
entries.legalExplanation: The case reversed lower reasoning but did not enter judgment holding asbestos victim permanently barred.
entries.examApplication: Always present both questions with separate headings on exam.
entries.examTrap: A claimant losing Frenville's argument does not necessarily lose lawsuit.
